purpose: lists who has access to the repository, its teams, and the bots that acted

--text.description: prints the stages as text, even on a terminal

--json.description: the stages as one JSON object: stages, then each stage's document under its name, null for one that could not be read

--jq.description: the same JSON, formatted by jq for a person

--stages.description: prints the stages, one per line, in order, the same over any workspace

--marks.description: prints a mark per stage, as one JSON object: null for each, as each is read again only on Refresh, kittui offering no Watch for a tab kit never marks

people.description: {login, name, role, kind}, keyed by the login: name null where the forge shows none; role the forge's own name for it, as GitHub's admin, write, or read, GitLab's owner, developer, or guest, and on Azure DevOps admin for a team's administrator, else member; kind user, bot, or, on Azure DevOps, group. GitHub shows it only to who may push, and a caller who may not is told so. GitLab names its members, those inherited and invited among them, each at the highest role any gives them; Azure DevOps the members of the project's teams, as teams reads them

teams.description: {team, name, role, members}, keyed by the team, GitHub's slug, GitLab's group path, Azure DevOps' name: role the access the team has, null on Azure DevOps; members their logins, null for a team the caller cannot see. The team links to its page. GitHub's need the read:org scope; GitLab's are the groups the project is shared with. Past 20 teams, or past 100 members of one, the document is limited, at the teams drawn

agents.description: {login, acted, last}, keyed by the login: acted what it did, commit, change, or review; last when it last did, in seconds since the epoch. The login links to its page, where the forge gives one, and GitHub gives none for a bot seen only in commits. GitHub reads the bots among the authors of the 100 newest commits on the default branch, and of the open changes and the 50 merged last, 100 open at most, and their reviews, in one request: a bot is a Bot account, or a login that ends [bot]; past 100 open changes, or 20 reviewers of one, the document is limited, at the bots drawn. GitLab's are its bot users among the members, acted null, last the day each last acted. Azure DevOps names no bots, and draws none
